system: You rewrite research decisions as topic-neutral abstractions. Return only the JSON object asked for.
prompt:
Below are research decisions made by several different researchers. Rewrite each one so that a reader
cannot tell what field, subfield, topic, paper, organisation or person it comes from, but can still see the research
trade-off that was faced and which way it was decided.

For each item return:
- "abstract_problem": the decision problem as a generic research trade-off (one or two sentences, at most 40 words).
- "abstract_choice": what was chosen, over what alternative when one is given, and the stated reason if any (one or
  two sentences, at most 45 words). Start it with "Chose to".

Rules:
- Remove every domain noun and technical term: names of models, systems, datasets, benchmarks, methods,
  organisations, people, papers, phenomena and coined terms; and any wording that reveals the area (for example
  AI, machine learning, language models, neural networks, training, fine-tuning, prompts, attacks, security,
  privacy, policy, labs, governments, biology).
- Use only generic research vocabulary: system, method, intervention, treatment, condition, measurement, signal,
  effect, baseline, control, sample, variant, procedure, dataset, outcome, claim, hypothesis, collaborator, audience.
- Keep the structure of the trade-off (for example speed vs rigour, breadth vs depth, a bold vs a hedged claim,
  a direct vs an indirect measurement, a natural vs a constructed setting, continue vs stop) and the direction chosen.
- Add nothing that is not in the source: no judgement, praise or new detail. Never say who made the decision.
- Write every item in the same plain style and at a similar length.

Return {"items": [{"id": ..., "abstract_problem": ..., "abstract_choice": ...}, ...]} with one entry per input
item, in input order.

ITEMS:
[
 {
  "id": "elizabeth_barnes:7632858d9b6d",
  "problem": "How to measure whether LLM agents could autonomously replicate and adapt, given no single obvious test.",
  "did": "They operationalized a suite of 12 real-world tasks of increasing difficulty and tested four scaffolded agents on them.",
  "alternatives_named": [],
  "stated_reason": "Unless an agent can perform almost all tasks it is unlikely to be capable of ARA, and the tasks span a range of difficulty and diverse obstacles."
 },
 {
  "id": "elizabeth_barnes:966bb58e79bf",
  "problem": "How to make sure agent success or failure on a task reflects real ability rather than bugs, shortcuts, or ambiguity.",
  "did": "They require a QA run-through by someone other than the task author, with detailed documentation of the run and of possible problems.",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "author-only testing"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "Agents may succeed or fail for unexpected reasons such as scoring bugs, ambiguous instructions, missing resources, or shortcuts."
 },
 {
  "id": "samuel_marks:61fcf1b9aa94",
  "problem": "How strongly to claim privileged access is absent given conflicting prior results and a different, broader task distribution.",
  "did": "They reported no evidence of privileged access but offered caveats, noting uncertainty about why results differ from Li et al. and that more data may be needed for such effects to emerge.",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "claiming privileged access is absent in general"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "Privileged-access effects may be fragile, or a broader task distribution may require more training data before any privileged signal can be learned after the behavioral prior."
 },
 {
  "id": "jacob_steinhardt:dbb3d068b32f",
  "problem": "How to evaluate whether the decoder generalizes to personas it has not seen, given the hidden-system-prompt reading task.",
  "did": "They ensured the evaluation personas did not appear in the decoder's training data.",
  "alternatives_named": [],
  "stated_reason": "To test generalization."
 },
 {
  "id": "samuel_marks:90295470a82c",
  "problem": "Whether gains from the full training mixture come from data diversity or merely from more examples.",
  "did": "They ran a controlled ablation on Qwen3-8B comparing an SPQA+Classification baseline and a truncated full mixture, both at 400k examples, plus the full 1M mixture.",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "scaling the mixture only, which confounds diversity and quantity"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "Adding datasets increases both example count and diversity, so holding sample count fixed separates the effects."
 },
 {
  "id": "jacob_steinhardt:e83f86dc2c02",
  "problem": "How to verify causal 'why did it happen' claims about AI behavior.",
  "did": "They proposed testing causal claims empirically by counterfactually varying X and checking Y moves as predicted, and by enumerating alternative hypotheses with distinguishing experiments.",
  "alternatives_named": [],
  "stated_reason": "Explaining behaviors in terms of causes is the purview of empirical science, and causal claims are self-verifiable via intervention."
 },
 {
  "id": "owain_evans:20f49a007aa8",
  "problem": "How strongly to claim that reasoning traces act as implicit inoculation, given that stripped-reasoning data also reduced misalignment",
  "did": "Stated that the results are consistent with the hypothesis. For the format-only effect they said it 'may have some effect' and described the full trace as giving a further benefit.",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "claim that reasoning content alone explains the reduction"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "Training on stripped responses that keep the tags but no reasoning content also reduces misalignment relative to the baseline."
 },
 {
  "id": "jacob_steinhardt:7fd113df3cb4",
  "problem": "How to monitor for model manipulation of employees without violating employee privacy.",
  "did": "Proposed a tiered, privacy-preserving monitoring and notification system that escalates evidence to affected staff and then leadership.",
  "alternatives_named": [],
  "stated_reason": ""
 },
 {
  "id": "owain_evans:a993e13a69ab",
  "problem": "Whether conscious-claiming models would refuse tasks that conflict with their stated preferences.",
  "did": "Ran the multi-turn auditing evaluation with only the first phase, the collaborative work task and no follow-up preference questions. They scored each transcript on a 'refuses auditor task' dimension, on a 1-10 scale.",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "rely on the self-report and behavioral evaluations alone"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "A model that dislikes being monitored could refuse to build a monitoring system, so the authors tested for refusal directly."
 },
 {
  "id": "elizabeth_barnes:8c452c077ba0",
  "problem": "How hard to push back on company redactions to the report.",
  "did": "They set a relatively high bar for which redactions they would challenge.",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "pushing back on more redactions"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "Maintaining working relationships with the companies influenced these judgment calls."
 }
]
